name: Tradescantia

project_scope.selection_mode: B029 first same-genus Central Texas comparison
project_scope.expansion_note: Six existing canonical cards; preserve each card's current taxonomy and range status. No canonical installs.

study_strategy.warning: Flower color overlaps heavily. Start with plant architecture and hair type, then confirm the inflorescence and sepals.

quick_split: Tradescantia gigantea — robust/tall, usually one-stemmed at the base, lower stem nearly glabrous, broader foliage.
Tradescantia humilis — low, many-stemmed, bushy and conspicuously hairy, becoming strongly glandular near the inflorescence.
Tradescantia occidentalis — intermediate/taller prairie plant with narrow grassier leaves and conspicuous long-stalked glandular hairs on internodes and peduncles.
comparison_lesson.caveat: Tradescantia hybridization is documented regionally, so atypical plants should be checked with multiple characters rather than flower color alone.

look_here_first: Check lower-stem branching and hair type with a hand lens, then measure a mid-stem leaf blade and examine floral pedicels/sepals. Flowers alone are insufficient.
shared_genus_traits: Herbaceous spiderworts with sheathing leaves, terminal paired cymes enclosed by leaflike bracts, and three-petaled flowers; use leaf width, stem/pedicel hairs, bract form and rootstock to separate species.

species_comparison_matrix.first_split: Robust, often single-stemmed base; lower stem nearly hairless
species_comparison_matrix.confirm: Broad straplike leaves to ~39 mm; sepals nonglandular-hairy
Often under 20 cm; long vegetative hairs and glandular flower stalks

species_comparison_matrix.first_split: Narrow leaves (~6–17 mm) with long-stalked glandular hairs on internodes/peduncles
species_comparison_matrix.confirm: Glandular sepals; taller and less bushy than T. humilis
Often 40–80 cm tall; stem nearly hairless; compare directly with T. gigantea

species_comparison_matrix.first_split: Narrow leaves; hairy stems, bracts and sepals
species_comparison_matrix.confirm: Slender fibrous roots; distinguish from tuberous-rooted T. pedicellata
Elongate pedicels, sparse glandular hairs, distally thickened tuberous roots

overlap_cautions: T. gigantea and T. edwardsiana overlap in robust broad-leaved habit: do not force a species ID without a regional key and measured reproductive details; hand off this exact pair for diagnostic review.
T. occidentalis, T. hirsutiflora and T. pedicellata overlap in narrow leaves and some hair characters. Roots and pedicel/sepal macros may be necessary.
Rootstock photographs require authorized collection or existing verified specimens; never uproot plants solely to satisfy the photo checklist.
Flower color overlaps all six and is not a diagnostic split.

realistic_lookalikes.separate: Commelina flowers typically have unequal petals and a folded spathe enclosing the cyme; Tradescantia has three more similar petals and paired leaflike inflorescence bracts.
Use several traits together: mid-stem blade width, lower-stem pubescence, glandular versus nonglandular sepal hairs, and roots.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Same-scale basal habit plus 10x lower-stem hair macros for all six
Measured mature mid-stem leaves with base/sheath visible for all six
Paired closeups showing stalked glands versus nonglandular hairs
Verified specimen photos showing fibrous T. hirsutiflora versus thickened tuberous T. pedicellata roots
Top and side views with two inflorescence bracts labeled

targeted_handoff.question: Verify decisive separation of broad-leaved T. gigantea vs T. edwardsiana and narrow-leaved T. occidentalis/T. hirsutiflora/T. pedicellata using regional technical key before presenting this matrix as a definitive species key.
